title: Lesson Plan — Quadratic Equations (Class 10 NIOS Mathematics)
subject: Mathematics
objectives: Identify a quadratic equation and write it in standard form ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0.
Verify whether a given value is a root by substitution.
Solve a quadratic by factorisation using the zero-product property.
Solve a quadratic by completing the square.
Apply the quadratic formula to any quadratic.
Use the discriminant to classify the nature of roots.
Translate a word problem into a quadratic and reject non-physical roots.
prerequisites: Chapter 4: Factorisation, especially split-the-middle for ax^2 + bx + c.
materials: Cards labelled with quadratics for a 'how to solve?' sort (factor / complete-the-square / formula)

activities.description: Recall starter. Write x^2 − 5x + 6 = 0 on the board. Ask: 'How many solutions does this have? Can you find them?' Take three answers; reveal that 2 and 3 both work (substitution). Then ask: 'Can a quadratic ever have NO solutions?' Collect guesses; promise the answer in the Explain phase via the discriminant.
teacher_actions: Pose the equation; collect three guesses.

activities.description: Pair card sort. Distribute cards (x^2 − 4 = 0, x^2 + 6x + 9 = 0, x^2 − x − 1 = 0, 2x^2 + 5x − 3 = 0, x^2 + 1 = 0). Pairs sort into 'factor easily', 'complete the square', 'use the formula', and 'no real roots' bins. The teacher uses the disagreements to launch the formal methods.
teacher_actions: Listen for the 'no real roots' verdict on x^2 + 1 = 0.
Pick a pair to share their categorisation.
student_actions: Tag any card they disagree on.

activities.description: Direct instruction in five blocks: (i) standard form + verification by substitution; (ii) factorisation with zero-product property and the worked example x^2 − 5x + 6 = 0; (iii) completing the square step-by-step on x^2 − 6x + 5 = 0; (iv) deriving the quadratic formula by completing the square on the general form; (v) discriminant cases with the parabola pictures, and sum/product-of-roots relations.
teacher_actions: Build the 5-step solving plan on the board.
Long-derive the quadratic formula live (key moment).
Sketch the three discriminant cases (parabola crosses, tangent, doesn't cross).
Drill the sum/product formulas: α + β = −b/a; αβ = c/a.
student_actions: Take notes; replicate every worked example.
Predict the next step before the teacher writes it.
Add the formula and discriminant cases to a 'rules box'.

activities.description: Application station. Students do six worksheet problems: one factorisation, one completing-the-square, one quadratic-formula, one discriminant classification, one sum/product-of-roots construction, one word problem.
teacher_actions: Circulate; offer the smallest hint that unblocks a stuck student.
Collect common slips for the Evaluate phase.
Pair fast finishers with peers who need support.
student_actions: Self-check against a posted answer key.

activities.description: Exit-ticket quiz: 8 questions drawn from the bank — at least one per outcome. Students complete silently in 8 minutes. Project the answers; 4-minute discussion of the two items most missed.
teacher_actions: Distribute exit ticket; remind students it is individual.
Tally results; address top two miss items.
student_actions: Self-mark and write a one-line reflection.

activities.description: Set homework: rest of the worksheet, plus one CREATE prompt — 'Construct a quadratic equation whose roots are the SQUARES of the roots of x^2 − 4x + 1 = 0; show your work.' Preview the next chapter (Arithmetic Progressions) by writing 2, 5, 8, 11, ... and asking what the 100th term is.
student_actions: Pack the worksheet and the formula reference card.

homework: Complete the remaining problems on the Worksheet — Quadratic Equations handout.
Construct a quadratic whose roots are the SQUARES of the roots of x^2 − 4x + 1 = 0; verify by substitution.
Find the value of k for which 2x^2 + (k − 1)x + 8 = 0 has equal roots; show your work.
assessment_ideas: Use the 8-item exit ticket as a quick formative check.
Set a 12-question quiz from the chapter bank for the next class as summative.
Mark the LONG_ANSWER on the rectangle-area word problem using the auto-grade rubric.
Run a 5-minute peer-grading round on the CREATE homework using a two-criterion rubric (correct construction? verification by substitution?).
references: NIOS Secondary Mathematics, Module 1, Lesson 6: Quadratic Equations.
NCERT Class 10 Mathematics, Chapter 4: Quadratic Equations (parallel coverage).
